name: Offline road routing (A*/Dijkstra) with distance, time and street list
description: Shortest or fastest route between two points (optionally through up to 8 via points) on a local road dataset, for car, walking or bike, using A* or Dijkstra. Returns distance, free-flow travel time, the street-by-street segments and a GeoJSON LineString ready for the map renderer. Answers "Kadıköy iskelesinden Moda'ya en kısa yol".

provenance.reference_values: Fixture graphs are synthetic (CC0). Expected vertex paths, distances and durations were produced by the installed networkx 3.6.1 (astar_path or dijkstra_path) on a DiGraph built from the same Skillpack graph builder; the harness checks that the installed astar.py and weighted.py are byte-identical to the pinned upstream copies under upstream/. Graph construction is shared code, so only the search is independently compared.

dataset.description: Dataset name (no folders), e.g. demo_kadikoy or my_pois.csv

budget.enforcement: Raw CLI byte limit and POSIX alarm; strict schema, finite values and nesting checks; MCP subprocess killed/reaped after 10 seconds. One active calculation. Not a hostile-code sandbox.

data.reads: local files by dataset name from SKILLPACK_MAP_DATA or ../map_data

mcp.instructions: Local offline map tool. The dataset is a file NAME inside the folder the user configured (SKILLPACK_MAP_DATA); never invent coordinates or names. Results come from the local data and code; explain them, state data limits (no live traffic) and ask the human to confirm before acting on them. Credit OpenStreetMap contributors when showing OSM-derived data.

limitations: Routing uses only the local road file: free-flow speeds by road class (car: motorway 90 ... residential 25, living street 10, service 15 km/h, or a numeric maxspeed tag), walking 5 km/h (steps 3), cycling 15 km/h (5 on footways that allow bicycles). One-way tags and roundabouts are respected for car and bike, ignored for walking; access=no/private roads are excluded. There is no live or historic traffic, no turn restrictions or turn costs, no traffic lights, ferries, public transport, elevation or time-of-day rules. Vertices are joined only where lines share an identical coordinate (7 decimals), as in OSM-derived exports; bridges/tunnels without shared nodes are not connected. Points are snapped to the nearest routable vertex (straight-line, default limit 300 m), which can be on the wrong side of a barrier. The whole file is read on every call; files above roughly 20 MB may not finish within the 10-second limit. Vertex numbers in the output are internal to one dataset load.
port_notes: The search is a port of networkx 3.6.1 astar_path (counter tie-break, enqueued/explored bookkeeping, skip of stale queue entries); Dijkstra is the same function with a zero heuristic, as in upstream. The heuristic is straight-line haversine distance (divided by the fastest edge speed in the graph when optimizing time), so it never overestimates and A* returns an optimal path. Graph building, snapping, profiles and segment grouping are Skillpack code in tool/mapdata.py and tool/main.py, documented in SKILL.md.
